typography.notes: Display font must convey authority, public works, and structure. Body font must be highly legible for dense operational data, resembling a city dashboard. No Inter for headings. Use tight tracking for headers.

colors.notes: Colors are strictly derived from the priority mapping constraint. The UI acts as a neutral canvas (Slate/White) to let the priority pins shine. No decorative gradients.

visual_enhancers.borders: 1px solid #E2E8F0 or #CBD5E1. Keep radii tight (2px to 4px max) for an industrial, structural feel. Avoid large pill shapes for structural cards.
visual_enhancers.shadows: Minimal. Use crisp, slight drop-shadows (shadow-sm) to lift map overlays instead of large diffuse glows.
visual_enhancers.textures: Clean, flat civic-tech aesthetics. Focus on data density and legibility.

layouts.landing_page: Map-hero layout. The map (live or image fallback) covers 100% of the viewport or acts as a massive split-screen. Opaque, high-contrast overlay card or left-sidebar for the core value prop and role selection. No centered generic hero blobs.
layouts.dashboard_ops: Split-view architecture. Left Sidebar (30-40% width): Role-based list queue sorted by priority. Right (60-70% width): Live map with priority-colored pins.
layouts.report_flow: Mobile-first, single-column focused form. Prioritize the camera/upload dropzone and location map picker with large touch targets. Do not overcomplicate.

components.buttons: Sharp edges or minimal radius (4px). High contrast. Primary buttons should be bg-slate-900 text-white with a visible focus state.
components.cards: Flat surfaces, 1px border. No excessive padding. Use technical bento-grid structures for metadata (time, lat/lng).
components.pins: Custom map markers explicitly using the priority colors. Include an inner visual indicator (dot or icon) to enhance color-blind accessibility.
components.tags: Small, uppercase, tracking-wider badges for status and priority. Use text-xs font-bold.

motion.pins: Subtle drop-in animation on the map on load.
motion.transitions: Instant or very fast (150ms) for UI panels. Civic ops tools need to feel snappy, responsive, and utilitarian, not 'floaty'.

accessibility.focus: High-contrast focus rings (ring-2 ring-slate-900 ring-offset-2) on all interactive elements. Visible keyboard focus states are mandatory.
accessibility.contrast: Ensure text inside priority tags (e.g., white text on Critical Red) strictly passes APCA/WCAG standards.

media.map_style: If embedding Google Maps, apply a muted JSON style (Silver or Grayscale). Do NOT use default saturated map colors; the map must serve as a subdued background so the 4 priority colors pop instantly.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build strictly within the YAGNI scope: Landing, Auth, Report Flow, Map Dashboard, Detail View. No extra pages.
Core models: Report and User only. Do NOT build admin settings, multi-language, notifications, gamification, or chat.
Design the entire app around the priority pin colors (critical/high/medium/low). The map must look like a real operational tool.
Ensure ALL interactive and informational elements have data-testid attributes (e.g., data-testid='report-submit-button').
Avoid transparent backgrounds in headers or overlays. Overlays must be solid or heavily blurred (backdrop-blur-xl) with high opacity.
For the Landing page, make the map the hero visually. Avoid standard SaaS landing page templates. Frame it as civic software.
Use Shadcn UI components (.js/.jsx) but heavily customize them to remove the 'default SaaS' look by enforcing sharp borders and tight metrics.
Write real, purposeful copy. No 'Lorem Ipsum'.
UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: Do not converge toward generic AI outputs. Build a civic-tech operational dashboard aesthetic.
Avoid centered generic hero layouts and simplistic gradients. Use dynamic, asymmetric, or split-screen structures.
Create depth with explicit z-index hierarchy and crisp shadows.
Use specific interaction transitions (e.g., transition-colors, transition-transform) rather than 'transition-all'.
Never apply text-align: center to the root App container.
Use sharp rectangular or slightly rounded buttons matching the industrial aesthetic, with clear hover animations.
Do not use emojis as icons. Use lucide-react icons.
Ensure generous but structured spacing (e.g., p-4 to p-8 internally for cards).
